title: Form, History and the Critic's Dilemma
text:
Literary criticism has long oscillated between two poles: the conviction that a text is a self-sufficient artefact, to be read closely for its internal patterns, and the view that it is inextricably bound to the historical and ideological circumstances of its production. The New Critics of the mid-twentieth century championed the former, insisting that the poem itself, rather than the poet's biography or intentions, was the proper object of analysis. Subsequent theorists, from Marxist critics to proponents of reader-response theory, argued that meaning is never simply contained within the page but is negotiated between the text and its interpreters.

This tension has never been fully resolved, and the most productive critical practices tend to hold both positions in uneasy suspension. A close reading of a sonnet, for instance, may reveal formal ambiguities that gain their significance only when situated within the conventions of the period in which it was written. Critics who ignore such context risk mistaking the peculiarities of their own era for universal truths. The ambition, therefore, is not to choose between formalism and historicism but to let each correct the other's blind spots.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what did the New Critics insist should be the proper object of analysis?
options: The poem itself, rather than the poet's biography or intentions
The historical circumstances in which the poet lived
The emotional response the poem provokes in its reader
The ideological aims of the publisher

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what example is given of formal ambiguities gaining significance?
options: A novel read without any reference to its author
A translation compared closely with its original
A close reading of a sonnet placed within the conventions of its period
A diary entry read for its psychological insight

questions.text: What can be inferred about critics who ignore historical context?
options: They are likely to mistake features of their own era for timeless truths
They produce more accurate readings than formalist critics do
They have abandoned the study of literary form altogether
They are chiefly interested in the private lives of authors

questions.text: Which conclusion about the writer's final position is best supported by the passage?
options: Formalism should be abandoned entirely in favour of historicism
Formal and historical approaches are most useful together, each checking the other's limits
The New Critics succeeded in resolving the tension between the two positions
Reader-response theory is the only defensible method of interpretation

vocabulary.definition: moved back and forth between two states or positions
in a way that cannot be separated or untangled
an object or work made by human craft or design
features that can be understood in more than one way

paragraph_translations: Krytyka literacka od dawna waha się między dwoma biegunami: przekonaniem, że tekst jest samowystarczalnym artefaktem, który należy czytać uważnie pod kątem jego wewnętrznych wzorców, a poglądem, że jest on nierozerwalnie związany z historycznymi i ideologicznymi okolicznościami swojego powstania. Nowi krytycy połowy XX wieku opowiadali się za pierwszym stanowiskiem, twierdząc, że właściwym przedmiotem analizy jest sam wiersz, a nie biografia poety ani jego zamierzenia. Późniejsi teoretycy, od krytyków marksistowskich po zwolenników teorii odbiorcy, dowodzili, że znaczenie nigdy nie zawiera się po prostu na stronie, lecz jest negocjowane między tekstem a jego interpretatorami.

To napięcie nigdy nie zostało w pełni rozwiązane, a najbardziej owocne praktyki krytyczne zwykle utrzymują oba stanowiska w niepewnym zawieszeniu. Dokładna lektura sonetu może na przykład ujawnić formalne dwuznaczności, które nabierają znaczenia dopiero wtedy, gdy umieści się je w kontekście konwencji epoki, w której powstał utwór. Krytycy, którzy ignorują taki kontekst, ryzykują pomylenie osobliwości własnej epoki z uniwersalnymi prawdami. Celem nie jest zatem wybór między formalizmem a historyzmem, lecz pozwolenie, by każde z tych podejść korygowało martwe punkty drugiego.
